open_questions: Centroid is inconclusive (verdict inconclusive, no sector with a clear difference image, centroid_all not_run) so on-sky location is not yet imaged, but no corrector neighbour exists to require it.

Duration ratio 1.47 is long for TIC radius 0.3867 but central_h 2.378 vs observed_h 3.5 still permits an off-centre/low-density transit for an M dwarf; star_density_penalty 46.97 remains a blemish that does not overturn the planet case.
dossier.public_summary: TESS shows a 3.5-hour, 3300-ppm flat-bottom dip every 14.6 days that repeats in two sectors with the same depth and no secondary or odd-even difference. At 2.4 Earth radii it is planet-sized and no nearby star in a TESS pixel can make a dip this deep. The look differs slightly from the training set that gave a low planet_rank, and the centroid image failed, so a ground-based transit remains the only test to prove it is on the M dwarf and not a background blend.

reasons.why: Planet-sized sub-Neptune; undiluted_depth_ppm 3364 with contratio 0.003481 rules out blend dilution, plausible_within_1px 0 and could_cause_within_1px 0 leaves no TESS-pixel neighbour that can fake the dip.
Flat-bottomed transit (negative v_sigma) with fit_b 0.1118 favours a planet over a grazing/v-shaped EB, despite duration.ratio 1.471.
No secondary eclipse (snr 1.887 <<5 and best_brightening_snr 2.849) argues against an eclipsing binary on the target.
Odd-even depths equal (3398 vs 3050 ppm, depth_ratio 1.1) disfavours an EB at twice the period.

Depth is constant between sectors (3597 ppm in sector 57 vs 3152 ppm in sector 84) and transit_depths p_consistent 0.829866485805048 with 3 transits shows signal is not from a few bad events; SNR 10.36/10.18 is above the 7 threshold.
